definition: Subjective idealism is a name used for the view, associated with Berkeley, that the material world has no independent substance and is real only as it is experienced by conscious beings. In this source, however, the label immaterialism is said to fit better because Berkeley still treats other minds, including a divine mind, as genuinely real.
